nodes.statement: A set A with a partial map - cdot_A - is a partial combinatory algebra (PCA) if there are elements combK, combS in PartA such that, for all u, v, w in PartA: &definedK, & &definedS,\\ &definedu lthen definedcombK \, u, & &definedu lthen definedcombS \, u, \\ &definedu land definedv lthen definedcombK \, u \, v, & &definedu land definedv lthen definedcombS \, u \, v, \\ &definedu land definedv lthen combK \, u \, v = u, & &definedu land definedv land definedw lthen definedcombS \, u \, v \, w, \\ && &definedu land definedv land definedw lthen combS \, u \, v \, w = (u \, w) \, (v \, w), \\
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:PCA}
  
  
  
  
  
  A set $A$ with a partial map ${-} \cdot_A {-}$ is a \emph{partial combinatory algebra (PCA)} if there are
  elements $\combK, \combS \in \Part{A}$ such that, for all $u, v, w \in \Part{A}$:
  
  \begin{align*}
    &\defined{K}, &
    &\defined{S},\\
    &\defined{u} \lthen \defined{\combK \, u}, &
    &\defined{u} \lthen \defined{\combS \, u}, \\
    &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \lthen \defined{\combK \, u \, v}, &
    &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \lthen \defined{\combS \, u \, v}, \\
    &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \lthen \combK \, u \, v = u, &
    &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \land \defined{w} \lthen \defined{\combS \, u \, v \, w}, \\
    &&
    &\defined{u} \land \defined{v} \land \defined{w}
     \lthen \combS \, u \, v \, w = (u \, w) \, (v \, w), \\
  \end{align*}
